label: sound

unstated.what: Behavior must also hold for paths with a leading slash (mkdir('/a/b'), touch('/a/b/c.d'), ls('/a')), which the instruction example never shows
unstated.quote:
m.mkdir("/a/b")
    m.touch("/a/b/c.d")
    listed = m.ls("/a")
    assert listed == ["/a/b/"]

unstated.what: detail=True entries must include type == 'directory' for the pseudo-directory

reasons: All hidden tests exercise the exact reported bug (duplicate directory listing after mkdir+touch) using the existing MemoryFileSystem API (store, pseudo_dirs, ls, mkdir, touch), whose output formats ('a/b/' strings and detail dicts) already exist in the code. Nothing extra is requested.

The hidden tests exercise only the reported duplication bug via existing ls/mkdir/touch APIs and pre-existing output formats; the leading-slash and detail variants are direct consequences of the same fix.

The core duplicate-listing bug, its output format, and the detail-mode name with trailing slash are all shown in the instruction. Only the leading-slash variant and the detail 'type' field are extra, and both are conventional/derivable consequences of normalizing paths in ls/mkdir/touch.
